Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Monitoring psychological impact of ongoing physical illness
- Patient Goal(s): Maintain positive mood and daily functioning while medical investigations proceed
- Clinical Goal(s): Detect early signs of mood or anxiety disorder; support coping strategies
- Actions (Patient): • Continue regular routine within energy limits • Engage in light exercise as tolerated • Monitor mood changes; report any persistent low mood, anhedonia, or heightened anxiety
- Actions (Clinician/GP): • Provide basic psychoeducation on mood monitoring • Reassess mental state at follow-up call after blood-test results • Offer standardized screening (e.g., PHQ-9/GAD-7) if symptoms emerge

Secondary Problem: Past stress/anxiety (in remission)
- Patient Goal(s): Prevent recurrence of stress-related symptoms
- Clinical Goal(s): Reinforce use of previous successful coping strategies
- Actions (Patient): • Resume proven stress-management techniques (e.g., walking, structured breaks) • Maintain work–life balance
- Actions (Clinician/GP): • Review coping strategies at next appointment • Consider referral to counseling/CBT if stress re-escalates

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Relationship between chronic physical symptoms and mood; signs of depression/anxiety; when to seek help
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Persistent low mood >2 weeks, loss of interest, sleep disturbance, increased irritability, thoughts of self-harm
- Coping Strategies: Graded exercise, relaxation/breathing techniques, maintaining social contact, structured daily schedule

Consent, Coordination & Review:

- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: None currently
